metadata.title: The Minimum Distance of Unshifted Spherical Fibonacci Lattices
metadata.description: For every Fibonacci number N=F_n>=2, we prove that the unshifted rational spherical Fibonacci lattice has least Euclidean distance2/sqrt(N), uniquely attained by the north pole and the next point. This answers the separation question in Brauchart's contribution to Oberwolfach Report40/2012,p2438 (UnsolvedMath OWR-12012-001). The proof combines a global Lambert-map distance inequality with Zaremba's classical formula for the Fibonacci lattice figure of merit. More generally, a rational N-point Lambert lift with Zaremba index rho>=N/4 has exactly this minimum; rho>N/4 also gives uniqueness. The construction includes a pole and uses the exact rational Fibonacci angle; the claim does not concern the different shifted irrational Fibonacci spiral, discrepancy, or optimal packing among all point sets. The four-page written proof is accompanied by symbolic and integer regression checks and separately labelled floating-point diagnostics. This is a self-audited, unrefereed preprint prepared with AI assistance, without independent review, formal proof-assistant verification, or an absolute-priority claim.

This research note proves the focal pedal area equality observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller in April 2020 for every primitive closed elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate elliptical caustic, including coprime star orbits. More precisely, the signed supporting-line pedal areas of the outer tangent polygon and the original chord polygon are proportional by a positive phase-independent constant common to both foci. A common pair of simple poles, local original and adjacent outer cancellations, strict real signed positivity, and compact-torus residue matching yield the proof. Reversal and positive integral repetitions are covered explicitly.

An exact triangular certificate disproves the interpretation that the common focal ratio itself is constant over the family. Prior observation of the equality, its known primitive-even symmetry proof, an explicit triangular consequence of old geometric theorems, the classical nonconstancy corollary, canonical coordinates and established Jacobi principal-part methods are credited. The specialized local arguments already appeared in companion repository work and are reconstructed here. A bounded primary-source priority audit identified no earlier proof across the full stated domain; no absolute firstness, independently new invariant, triangular novelty, new negative theorem, or new general method is claimed. Hyperbolic or collapsed caustics, diameter walks, unsigned lobe areas and segment-clamped projections are excluded.

The supporting archive contains the editable standalone source, the conditional triangular deduction, exact and finite high-precision verification programs, actual outputs, provenance and source/edition limitations. Numerical diagnostics are not interval-certified and do not replace the universal proof. This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively for proof development, literature comparison, computation, reproduction, writing and independent adversarial verification. Internal AI reviews are not external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification; neither is claimed.

metadata.title: Loss of total-space positivity for the normalized relative Kähler–Ricci flow
metadata.description:
We give a negative answer to the total-space positivity-preservation question for the probability-normalized relative Kähler–Ricci flow defined by Naumann on O_E(r). For E = O(1) ⊕ O(1) over the projective line, a smooth strictly positive initial metric on O_E(2) = O(2,2) evolves to horizontal curvature exactly −1/96 at time (log 2)/2. The four-page research note proves global initial positivity and derives the exact second-variation evolution along a stationary central fiber.

The flow construction was already known; the result addresses the explicit positivity question in the original report and published article, rather than the Griffiths conjecture or other normalizations. The deposit includes manuscript source, reproducible exact verification, independent mathematical audits, and a bounded primary-source priority audit. Historical first priority is not asserted; a relevant 2025 Naumann habilitation was identified but its text was not recovered. Smooth finite-time flow existence is a cited analytic input, not a computational conclusion.

AI tools were used extensively in development, writing, reproduction, and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with internal AI adversarial reviews; it has not received human peer review.
